findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The new absence test asserts that the producer brief still contains `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`. The only producer-brief source of that text is the section being deleted.
findings.evidence: Grep of 'cargo test -p <crate>' over crates/ finds it in producer-brief code only at briefs.rs:770, inside time_budget_section. The other hits are prompts/producer.md:9 (a prompt, not the brief), briefs.rs:815-817 ('--test <name>', '<module>') and briefs.rs:1172 ('<name>'). Once time_budget_section is removed, that 'present' assertion fails. The current pin at briefs.rs:2081 only passes because the section exists. Fix: Drop the `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>` presence assertion. If the test needs a positive check, assert that the no_change section heading ('## If you leave the tree unchanged') or a phrase from checks_before_verifier_section is present. Also fix Decision 3's wording, which implies the brief keeps the targeted-test advice: only producer.md:9 keeps it.

findings.summary: A correct 'problem already gone' result ends as a Failed outcome with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX, and introspection handles it as a failure. The plan lists introspect.rs but does not say what follows from this.
findings.evidence: introspect.rs:1546-1577 turns every OutcomeState::Failed outcome into an IntrospectionTrigger::Failure event with category 'failed' and sets planning_stopped from the reason prefix. The producer fallback (no_change already_done) also ends Failed (candidate.rs no_change_reason). Both paths record a stale fix the same way as a real planning failure. Fix: Keep the design: a new outcome state is out of scope. Add a risk saying a 'No change:' stop is recorded as a failed planning stop and is introspected and counted as a failure. Say the same in the CHANGELOG entry so the owner knows how to read these outcomes.
findings.location: Decision 5 / Dependents entry 'The planning stop that a No change: plan ends in' (introspect.rs:1577)

findings.summary: A 'No change:' plan must still pass admission's checks on behavior criteria, but the bullet asks only for a demonstration that 'cites that evidence'.
findings.evidence: admission.rs:207-242 sends back (Major) any demonstration of a behavior criterion that has an empty fails_without, an empty seam, or a command the verifier may not run. planner.md:10 covers the seam and the command but not fails_without. If a 'No change:' plan leaves fails_without empty, it uses up MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES (planning.rs:521). The job then stops with a mechanical reason instead of the critic's summary, so the reason the problem is gone is lost. Fix: Within the byte cap, end the bullet with something like '...one demonstration that cites that evidence, with the usual fields.' Or confirm that the schema already forces fails_without for every demonstration and cite where.

findings.summary: The planner cannot tell a 'queued fix' from any other job, because nearly every job is queued.
findings.evidence: PlannerInputs (planner.rs:33-45) has no field that marks a job as a queued fix. Only a revision or retry seed is visible to the planner. In practice the planner will apply the rule to any request that reads as a fix. Fix: Phrase the trigger by what the planner can see, for example '- A request to fix a problem, or a retry: first check ...'. The bytes stay about the same.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot using Read and Grep. It matches the accepted reading and the code. Every place the plan names exists where it says: DEADLINE_RULE and deadline_section (planner.rs:94-115, call at 181), PlannerInputs.deadline_s (planner.rs:44), time_budget_section (briefs.rs:758-776, call at 696), ProducerInputs.deadline_s (briefs.rs:373) and the literals the plan lists. The enforced limits stay: agent_spec still gets timeout_s at planning.rs:175 and producer_deadline_s at producer.rs:363. A Grep of deadline_s and of the section text finds no reader the dependents list leaves out. Of the old test names, only CHANGELOG history mentions them. The stale-fix path is sound: plan_findings (admission.rs:177-320) puts no check on an empty files list, JobPlan::validate accepts it, and on reject end_round calls stop_planning with the critic's summary (planning.rs:8-14, 491-505). The lifecycle helpers the new test uses all exist (lifecycle.rs:3221-3299). The extra critic-brief rule is small, sits in a listed deliverable, and gives the planner rule a real end state. Four minor problems remain. (1) One planned "present" assertion would fail: the only producer-brief source of that text is the section being removed. (2) The "No change" end state is recorded as a Failed planning stop, which introspection treats as a failure. (3) The bullet does not remind the planner that admission's behavior-criterion fields still apply. (4) "Queued fix" is a vague trigger. None of these stops a criterion from being shown, so the verdict is accept.
